data.full_response: Crucible is a knowledge-grounded agent runtime where markdown notes, sessions, and wikilinks form a knowledge graph that agents draw from and contribute to. It follows a Neovim-like architecture: a headless daemon (`cru daemon serve`) owns all storage and business logic over JSON-RPC 2.0 on a Unix socket, while thin clients (TUI, REPL, web) handle only rendering and input.

data.content:
on the docs kiln:

**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open standard for connecting AI models to external
tools and data sources. It defines a uniform interface so any AI agent can discover and call tools, read resources, and access context

— Crucible uses it to aggregate tools from upstream MCP servers under prefixed namespaces.

**ACP (Agent Client Protocol)** is an
open protocol for AI agent hosting. It defines how a host application spawns, manages, and communicates with external AI agents (like Claude Code, OpenCode
, Gemini CLI) over stdio JSON-RPC — Crucible uses it to delegate
work to those agents while controlling trust and depth limits.

data.full_response:
Based on the docs kiln:

**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. It defines a uniform interface so any AI agent can discover and call tools, read resources, and access context — Crucible uses it to aggregate tools from upstream MCP servers under prefixed namespaces.

**ACP (Agent Client Protocol)** is an open protocol for AI agent hosting. It defines how a host application spawns, manages, and communicates with external AI agents (like Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI) over stdio JSON-RPC — Crucible uses it to delegate work to those agents while controlling trust and depth limits.
